fixed.how: New session/recovery.ts. recoverInterruptedSessions runs in compose.ts after intake.closeExpired (opts.recoverSessions, which defaults on with services and is never on in a CLI one-shot). It ends every running or paused work session of the human's agents that has no live kill-switch registration, skipping intake, cloud and other-device sessions. Each one ends 'stopped' with stop_reason 'interrupted' and the summary "Interrupted: Forerunner closed while this session ran. \"X\" is ready again.". Its running runs are closed, its claimed or in_progress tasks go back to Ready with the reason 'Forerunner closed while it ran', and one Update is posted. POST /sessions/:id/stop on a row nothing runs ends it the same way (endDeadSession, reason 'Stopped by you'). The runner's one-session refusal now says it in words with no uuid. SessionView gains stopReason and statusText ('Interrupted: Forerunner closed'), and the session page badge shows statusText. An ended session no longer shows a current task.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Start a session on a project. While a task runs, end the daemon hard (kill the process, or scripts/bench/restart-daemon.mjs --hard). Reopen the app. The old session's page reads 'Interrupted: Forerunner closed' with 'no task running'. The task is Ready on the Tasks tab, the Inbox has one line 'Your last session was interrupted when Forerunner closed. "…" is ready again.', and the next Start works the first time with no 409.

fixed.problem: [major] A session ran only the tasks that were ready when it started: a 7-task chain took 7 Starts. Critic send-backs and retries waited for the next manual Start, which took 4 Starts to reach the sign-off card.

fixed.how: runner.ts now works off a queue. When the queue is empty, replan() reads readyTasks again with the sandbox gate and goes through the same Planner, so the first-session order and the handover seed-only plan still hold. It cuts the plan to what is left of the work budget and takes tasks that became ready, critic send-backs (the next attempt in the same session) and tasks the person made ready. The session row's plan grows with a versioned setPlan and a session.replanned event. Tasks skipped for a peer, a claim, the usage limit or the sandbox are not taken again in the same session. Autonomy 0 and 1 only re-run approved tasks. MAX_RUNS_PER_TASK_IN_SESSION=6 is a guard. A sent-back task is counted once in retried. The session stops when nothing runnable is left, the budget is used, the person stops it, or the wall clock runs out.
fixed.check_in_the_app: Approve a plan of 7 tasks that each wait on the one before (bench: FORERUNNER_BENCH_PLAN=chain) and press Start once. All 7 tasks run in that one session. With FORERUNNER_BENCH_CRITIC_REJECT='quote list', that step runs twice in the same session and ends done.

tests_changed_for_design.why: They asserted the old summary text: counts, 'Nothing to plan', USD 'Left out for budget', 'Moved by you…', 'Read before the session-end writes'. They also expected stopReason 'completed' for an empty session and the Inbox summary starting 'Session '. Each now asserts the design's lines or the one-line Update, and 'nothing_runnable' for an empty session. sandbox-waiting asserts the step on the one Docker card and runs per specialist.
The one-session refusal no longer shows 'already has an active session <uuid>' (§4.10); it expects 'is already working in another session'.
ADR 0102: a monthly schedule never runs on the day an install first sees it. Tests of a due-day run now sight the schedule earlier.
The calibration's session row is the critic agent's, not the principal's (ADR 0102).
The Inbox gets one Update line naming the project, and the result is 3 lines. The good day's sign-off task now counts as finished work for notes.

One Start climbs the whole ladder (sessions === 1). Runs of one session share the simulated clock, so they are counted by specialist and model. The H.5 cross-session pattern uses a second session on a task of the same kind.

With in-session rework a resolved finding's lesson lands the same day, so with memory no finding repeats in a later session. The gate now asserts the repeat rate never rises and ends at 0, and that findings per review drop week over week. The control must repeat more in every week. criticLessons with memory is 0, since no cross-session repeat exists; H.5 is covered in phase 3 and loop-critic. RecordingPlanner keeps one brief per session because re-plans reuse it.
Run artifacts now also keep the specialist's redacted report for the next attempt's brief (§4.6).
The single Stop becomes 'Stop after this task' plus 'Stop now' (asks once), and the badge shows statusText ('Working', 'Done', 'Stopped by you') instead of raw status (§3.7).

The Start dialog now says what runs, fills in the default budget, refuses bad budgets and blocked starts before sending, sends 'note' instead of 'reason', and keeps the person on the page with 'Open the session' instead of navigating (§3.6).
The result no longer echoes the person's own Cancel ('Moved by you while it ran…', §5.11); it asserts the 2-line result.

blocking.issue: The app's own Stop all (the header button), as well as Chat's stop and the phone's remote stop, still ends a running session as an error. The session log gets a red line "error  Error: killed session stopped during task" (the design's own "before" text). The stop reason is the raw "killed", the badge reads just "Stopped", and the result and the Inbox Update name no stop at all ('"Write one.html" and "Write two.html" are ready to continue. CHF 0.00.'). Cause: personStopOf recognises only the default reason strings, but the UI sends its own. Shell.tsx:103 posts POST /kill with reason "stop all from the UI"; server.ts:1435 passes body.reason through; personStopOf (stop-words.ts:22-27) matches only "kill switch from the app", "stopped from the app" and /^kill switch/i. So the runner falls back to stopReason=code ("killed") and emits session.error. The fixer's claim that Stop all becomes stop_all and session.stopped is therefore false on the path a person uses. No test drives a running session with the reason the UI really sends (validation rule 1): the tests use the STOP_ALL_REASON constant.

new_problems: The /changes/:id/undo route (server.ts commands section, session-engine) does not emit 'inbox' after an undo. Any undo that reopens a card, or changes requests in another way, leaves the header count stale until the next event or poll. The Tasks tab works around it by re-reading /inbox after its own Undo.

The critic's retry card (kind 'approval', change_card reason 'retry_ladder_exhausted', packages/runtime/src/loop/critic.ts:418) makes its task read 'Needs your answer' with 'Go ahead without' offered. Going ahead queues a 'without answering the questions' note, which does not fit a retry decision. Evidence: /tmp/frbench/fixup-tasks-screen/walk5.out ('Broken step in the build … Answer / Go ahead without / Cancel'). For needs-me (wave 2).

When a session's runs of a task share one millisecond (only with a frozen SimulatedClock in tests), pairReports cannot order them except by random id bits. Real clocks never tie: a run includes model calls and a critic review. The real-daemon drawer test therefore uses a moving clock (ShiftedClock, a system clock moved to 5 March so the monthly calibration of the 1st does not hold the agent). Adding the run id to the task.finished/task.files payloads in runner.ts (session-engine) would make the pairing exact.
